hypothesis: Adding one generic lattice-region map/reduce primitive family to the validated rule-first IR will recover exact candidate coverage on at least one of the two ARC-R030 diagnostic tasks without changing model, prompt budget, attempts, or scorer.

baseline.ir: schema-v1 global dihedral + global recolor only

primary_change: Extend the rule-first IR with a generic lattice-region map/reduce family supporting inferred repeated-cell partitions, peer aggregation, generic conditional writes, and reassembly; no task-specific coordinates/colors/patterns.

frozen_controls.scoring: deterministic execution + exact candidate-oracle coverage + comparator-integrity boundary

implementation_gate: Before any target-model call, unit tests must prove lattice inference, region extraction/reassembly, peer aggregation, conditional-write semantics, fail-closed validation, and absence of task IDs/absolute task-specific constants in the primitive implementation.
success_threshold: 2/2 parseable and >=1/2 mechanically verified exact candidate coverage, with no comparator mismatch.
falsification_conditions: 2/2 parseable but 0/2 exact candidate coverage after the richer IR is available to the model
the primitive requires task-specific coordinates, colors, or target-pattern constants to pass tests
secondary_diagnostics: which primitive operators appear in generated candidates
candidate diversity by normalized program AST
input/output tokens, calls, cache hits, runtime, provider failures
per-task exact coverage and executed-output diffs
resource_requirements: authorized NVIDIA NIM execution path for the eventual matched model ablation
anti_overfit_constraints: no task IDs in solver code or prompt
no fixed absolute coordinates for the two diagnostics
no task-specific color constants or hand-entered target patterns
